description:
Two pseudonymous identifiers, which is all the entity-link sample needs. Both carry a real hash rather than a placeholder: the column accepts 32 to 128 lowercase hex characters and refuses anything else, because accepting a non-hash would put a raw phone number into the column every downstream consumer treats as safe.

The hashes here are sha256 of a fixed sample string, so the file is reproducible and obviously synthetic. A real salt lives in configuration and never in a repository.

metadata_json.note: Shared by the collector and the pass-through account. One device hash in an overlapping window is what turns two accounts into a connected component, and it is the single most load-bearing record in the sample set.

Shared by three accounts on one day, one of which is the hard negative. A carrier NAT puts thousands of unrelated people behind one address, which is why links through an IP are inferred rather than deterministic and why one of the three was rejected on review.
